obligation: Acquirer notice of suspected card data compromise (contractual)
citation: Merchant agreement with the acquiring bank (fictional term); PCI DSS v4.0.1 Requirement 12.10.1 (N44-45-R01)
trigger: Suspected or confirmed compromise of card data, including a tamper detection alert on a payment page or a common point of purchase notice from the acquirer or processor
deadline: Within 24 hours of suspecting a compromise (merchant agreement term); then follow the acquirer's and card brands' instructions
notify: Acquirer merchant risk contact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not law

obligation: Visa report of suspected or confirmed compromise (contractual)
citation: Visa Core Rules and Visa Product and Service Rules (April 2026), 10.3.1.2 (ID# 0007999)
trigger: Suspected or confirmed loss, theft, compromise, or misuse of Visa account or cardholder information, systems, or equipment, including by a merchant
deadline: Immediately, in the format the What To Do If Compromised guide specifies (the guide itself is not restated here)
notify: Visa, through the acquirer; in the US region a merchant may report on the member's behalf
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - binds the acquirer, passed to the company by the merchant agreement

obligation: Visa forensic investigation duties (contractual)
citation: Visa Core Rules and Visa Product and Service Rules (April 2026), 10.3.1.1 (ID# 0007123)
trigger: Visa requires an investigation of a suspected or confirmed compromise
deadline: As Visa and the acquirer specify; give Visa, its agent, and any PCI Forensic Investigator (PFI) access to premises, records, systems, and forensic reports, and engage a PFI when required
notify: Acquirer and Visa; PFI engaged through counsel
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual
owner: PCI Program Manager with the General Counsel

obligation: Other card brands: American Express verified; Mastercard and Discover not verified (contractual)
citation: American Express Data Security Operating Policy (DSOP), United States, April 2026, Section 3. Mastercard and Discover rules, applied through the acquirer, not verified: Mastercard's site returned HTTP 403 and no Discover rules page was found. Not law
trigger: Suspected or confirmed compromise of American Express, Mastercard or Discover card data (for American Express, a potential or confirmed compromise is a Data Incident)
deadline: American Express: immediately, and no later than 72 hours after discovery; then investigate, and engage a PCI Forensic Investigator within 5 days of discovery if 10,000 or more card numbers are involved (DSOP Section 3). Mastercard and Discover: per the acquirer's instructions (not verified)
notify: American Express Enterprise Incident Response Program (EIRP@aexp.com, 1-888-732-3750), with a named company contact; Mastercard and Discover through the acquirer; Discover directly where the company has a direct merchant agreement
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - follow acquirer instructions; Mastercard and Discover rules were not verified

obligation: Processor notice (hosted payment fields and token vault)
trigger: Incident on pages that host the processor's payment fields, or any suspected exposure of tokens or processor credentials
deadline: Per agreement (standard term: notice within 24 hours of suspicion, fictional)
notify: Primary processor security contact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual

obligation: State breach notice to individuals (each state of residence)
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of personal information of residents, as each state defines it (card number with security code, or online account credentials, are covered in many states)
deadline: Varies by state: some say without unreasonable delay; some set a fixed number of days
notify: Affected residents of each state
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - apply the law of each state where affected individuals reside; outside counsel's state matrix
clock_starts: Varies by state (often determination of a breach)
owner: Chief Privacy Officer with outside counsel

obligation: State attorney general or regulator notice
trigger: Breach above a state-set count of residents, or any breach in some states
deadline: Varies by state
notify: State attorney general or other designated regulator
applies_at_this_tier: Yes where the state requires

obligation: State consumer reporting agency notice
trigger: Notices above a state-set count
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Nationwide consumer reporting agencies
applies_at_this_tier: Yes where the state threshold is met

obligation: State third-party agent (vendor) notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: A vendor that maintains personal information for the company (for example a script supplier or the processor) has a breach
deadline: Varies by state; company contracts require 24 hours for TPSPs (POL-03 4.12)
notify: The company (Director of Third-Party Risk Management)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - track in contracts (POAM-003)

obligation: Florida notice to individuals (worked example)
trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents. Personal information includes a name with a credit or debit card number and any required security code, and a user name or email address with a password for an online account (501.171(1)(g))
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and without unreasonable delay, no later than 30 days after the determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (15 more days on written good cause to the Department, for this notice only)
notify: Each affected Florida resident, by mail or email
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - expected for skimmed cards with security codes
clock_starts: Determination of a breach or reason to believe one occurred

obligation: Florida law enforcement delay (worked example)
trigger: A law enforcement agency determines that notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay for the period the agency specifies in writing; the agency may extend or revoke it in writing
notify: Hold individual notices; keep the written request
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if requested

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs (worked example)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 30 days after the determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (the 15-day extension does not apply to this notice)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (synopsis, number of Floridians, services offered, copy of the notice, contact)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents
clock_starts: Determination of a breach or reason to believe one occurred

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies (worked example)
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (timing, distribution, and content of the notices)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 1,000

obligation: Florida no-notice determination (worked example)
trigger: After investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the company reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Document the determination in writing, keep it at least 5 years, and provide it to the Department within 30 days after the determination
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs
applies_at_this_tier: Unlikely for skimmed card data with security codes; counsel decides

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice to the company (worked example)
trigger: Breach of a system maintained by a third-party agent (for example a script supplier or a TPSP)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 10 days after the agent's determination of the breach or reason to believe one occurred
notify: The company
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - vendors holding Florida residents' personal information

obligation: SEC materiality determination
trigger: Cybersecurity incident discovered that could be material
deadline: Without unreasonable delay after discovery (the disclosure committee convenes within 48 hours under POL-03 4.4)
notify: Disclosure committee (General Counsel chairs); record the date and time of the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SEC registrant

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 filing
trigger: The company determines a cybersecurity incident is material
deadline: Within 4 business days after the materiality determination
notify: SEC (public filing): material aspects of the nature, scope, and timing, and the material impact or reasonably likely material impact, including on financial condition and results of operations
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SEC registrant

obligation: SEC filing delay on Attorney General determination
trigger: U.S. Attorney General determines disclosure poses a substantial risk to national security or public safety and notifies the SEC in writing
deadline: Up to 30 days after the original due date; up to 30 more days on a further determination; in extraordinary circumstances a final period of up to 60 days (national security only)
notify: Department of Justice (through outside counsel); SEC notified by the Attorney General
applies_at_this_tier: Only if the Attorney General so determines

obligation: SEC annual cybersecurity disclosure
trigger: Annual report on Form 10-K
deadline: With the next Form 10-K; update the description of processes and of any material effects of incidents
notify: SEC (Form 10-K)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SEC registrant

obligation: Insider trading blackout
trigger: Disclosure committee convenes on a possibly material incident
deadline: Same day the committee convenes
notify: Committee members, incident responders with knowledge, and executives (special blackout notice)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - company policy, not a regulatory deadline

obligation: Law enforcement report (voluntary)
trigger: Criminal compromise of card data
deadline: As early as practical (supports investigation; may lead to a Florida 501.171(4)(b) delay request)
notify: U.S. Secret Service field office or FBI (IC3)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - voluntary

obligation: Cyber insurance notice
trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy; call the carrier's breach hotline before engaging vendors
notify: Carrier
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual

obligation: SL-1 and SL-2 client notices
citation: Retail media and supplier portal client agreements (contract)
trigger: Incident affecting client data or the SL-1 or SL-2 service
deadline: Per client agreement (standard term: 72 hours after confirming an incident that affects client data, fictional)
notify: About 140 CPG brand clients (SL-1); about 1,400 suppliers (SL-2)
applies_at_this_tier: Only if client data or those services are affected; not expected for checkout skimming
owner: Vice President, Retail Media; Vice President, Supplier Collaboration

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any extortion payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (2021-09-21); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Any extortion or ransom payment is considered
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license request if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Only if an extortion demand is made. All U.S. persons

obligation: SNAP EBT reporting to state agencies or FNS
citation: State retailer agreements and third party processor terms (7 CFR 274.3(c), (d))
trigger: Incident affecting store EBT terminals, the payment switch EBT routing, or EBT transaction data
deadline: Per state agreement and processor certification terms (not verified)
notify: State EBT agency or processor
applies_at_this_tier: No for this scenario - online SNAP is not offered and EBT card data never passes through the web checkout; applies if store EBT systems are involved

obligation: FTC Safeguards Rule notification event
trigger: Notification event at a financial institution involving 500 or more consumers
deadline: As soon as possible, no later than 30 days after discovery
notify: FTC via online form
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company issues no credit and is not a financial institution under Part 314 (P03)

obligation: CIRCIA incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after a ransom payment
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; reporting is voluntary until it takes effect

obligation: Covered telecommunications or Kaspersky article discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-25 and 52.204-23; FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Covered equipment or a Kaspersky covered article found in use
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification for covered telecommunications equipment or services (52.204-25(d)); within 3 business days for a Kaspersky covered article (52.204-23(c)); further report within 10 business days in both cases. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
notify: Contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: No - no federal contracts identified; recheck if contracts are signed
